why.reasoning: The catalog lists the two specializations as separate free-text placeholders, which made both look required. Students complete one, so they are now a choice of one. Forestry: field program ESPM 105A-D; 'ESPM 102B & 102BL or ESPM C110A'; ESPM 108A, 134, 182, 185; 'ESPM 102D or ESPM 60*'; and 'Electives 6-8 Units. Two courses from the following:'. The department's elective list adds ESPM C110A, ESPM C130 (Terrestrial Hydrology) and GEOG C183 to the catalog's list. The catalog's ESPM 130A and ESPM 190 are kept because the department doesn't exclude them explicitly. NRM, 'Two Options (Choose A or B)': 'Choice A: Select ONE field studies experience' (ESPM 105A-D, ESPM C107, or 'BIO/ENVS 188' UCNRS CA Ecology, which is ENVSCI 188 'Calif Ecology & Conservation' in the catalog; no BIOLOGY 188 exists) plus 'Three additional electives approved by NRM affiliated Faculty (see list below)'. Choice B: the quoted six-course concentration 'with at least one elective from each of the following categories', encoded as one course from each of the four category lists plus two more from any of them. The category lists combine the catalog and the department snapshot. The department adds ESPM 115B, ESPM C130, ESPM 139A and ESPM C162A (the catalog's ESPM 162A is kept too). It lists ESPM 162 under Value & Policy, not Management (where the catalog put it), so it was moved. Evaluator workaround: GradTrak counts courses greedily across every sub-rule, even in options a student doesn't pursue. If the Forestry and Choice A rules consumed courses, they would take courses from NRM/Choice B students, and the reverse. So the Forestry and Choice A sub-rules are `shared` (they re-read all courses), and Choice B is the exact path. This is a workaround, not a department double-counting allowance. See the log for the consequences.
